key_insight: DenseNet121 led ten pretrained models in classifying benign versus malignant breast histopathology images, achieving 99.4% test accuracy and 0.999 AUC-ROC.
clinical_relevance: Explainable image classification could support breast pathology assessment, but these results do not establish readiness for clinical use.
method: Benchmarked ten ImageNet-pretrained CNN and transformer models on BreakHis.
Used a patient-level split for benign-versus-malignant classification.
Applied Grad-CAM, LIME, Integrated Gradients, and LRP to visualize prediction-relevant regions.
evidence_signal: On the BreakHis test set, DenseNet121 reportedly outperformed all other models (p < 0.001), while explanations highlighted nuclei-rich and glandular regions.
watch_item: External validation is not reported in the abstract, leaving generalizability across institutions and imaging workflows uncertain.
paper_title: Interpretable Deep Learning Models for Breast Cancer Diagnosis Using Medical Imaging
